subject: music

moments.title: Jazz emerges in New Orleans
moments.body: African American musicians draw on blues, ragtime, marching band, opera and church traditions to develop new improvisatory practices.
moments.takeaway: Jazz arose at the intersection of multiple traditions in a multilingual port city.

moments.title: First jazz recording
moments.body: A white New Orleans group makes the first commercially released jazz record before any African American jazz band.
moments.takeaway: Industry structures shaped whose innovations reached recorded history first.

moments.title: Kind of Blue
moments.body: Davis's modal jazz album becomes one of the best-selling jazz records of all time, shifting harmonic practice away from chord-change-driven improvisation.
moments.takeaway: A single album can redirect a tradition's harmonic language.

now.title: Jazz today
now.body: Jazz exists in conservatory programmes, festival circuits and ongoing creative experiment. Hip-hop, funk and electronic genres draw on its harmonic vocabulary.
now.open_questions: How are improvisational practices being reshaped by digital tools and global collaboration?

reflection: Recovering the history of who created jazz, and who got credit, is itself an active scholarly and curatorial project.
